storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Welcome to Bea’s library. Our book is The Library of Little Things.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> I’d use that tiny whisk to stir a puddle as big as my kitchen.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: If you borrowed the tiny whisk, what adventure would you take it on?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Bea opened a library on her front steps. On the shelf sat a smooth stone, a tiny whisk, and a button shaped like a star.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Borrow a little thing,” said Bea. “Bring back a story.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Tavi borrowed the smooth stone. He brought it back warm from his pocket.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “My paper boat kept tipping, so I gave it a stone to sit on. We sailed all the way to the far side of the puddle.”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <gasp> That paper boat looks huge in the puddle!

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Can I pretend to sail it? Point where I should go, around a leaf or straight across?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: You can be the captain. Tavi borrowed the smooth stone. He used it to help his paper boat stay steady.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Zella borrowed the tiny whisk. She brought it back with a yellow ribbon tied to the handle.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I waved it to whisk up the wind. The wind lifted my kite right over the rooftops.” <gasp>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Idris borrowed the star button. He brought it back in his cupped hands.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I held it up when the moon looked lonely. Then I watched the whole sky fill with friends.” <sigh>

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: If I borrowed that star button, I’d take it on a night walk.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Can you add one thing we’d see? What did Idris see when he held up the button?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: He held up the little star button. Then he watched the sky fill with stars, like friends for the moon.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Bea put the three little things back on the shelf. “Borrow a little thing,” she said.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Idris reached for the whisk, Zella took the stone, and Tavi picked up the star. “We’ll bring back a story,” they said.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> I’d lend my spoon. I’d love to hear it went digging for treasure.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: What everyday thing would you lend, and what story would you love to hear when it comes back?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Thanks for reading with us. Subscribe and come back for our next story.
